title: Heroes of Faith
subtitle: Men and women of the Old Testament

guide.summary: The patriarchs Noah, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph are examples of persevering faith. Despite their fears and weaknesses, they trusted in God's calling. Their lives reveal how God works through generations, fulfilling His promises even when everything seemed impossible.

keyVerses.text: By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed by going out to a place which he was to receive for an inheritance; and he went out, not knowing where he was going. By faith he lived as an alien in the land of promise, as in a foreign land.
Now the Lord said to Abram, 'Get out of your country, away from your relatives, and away from your father's house, to a land that I will show you. I will make you into a great nation.'
Then some Midianite traders passed by, so they pulled Joseph up and lifted him out of the pit, and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver.

guide.summary: Moses and Joshua led God's people in critical moments. Moses was chosen to free Israel from Egypt through powerful miracles; Joshua conquered the promised land. Both trust in God against impossible odds, revealing that our limitations do not limit God.

So the people shouted, and the priests blew the trumpets. It happened, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, that the people shouted with a great shout, and the wall fell down flat.

guide.summary: Deborah, Gideon, Ruth, Samuel, and David exemplify diverse leadership in the period of judges and kings. Each responded to the calling in unique ways: as a warrior prophetess, reluctant warrior, loyal widow, intercessor prophet, and king after God's own heart. Their confrontations with physical enemies reveal greater spiritual battles.

keyVerses.text: Barak said to her, 'If you will go with me, then I will go; but if you will not go with me, I will not go.' She said, 'I will surely go with you; however, the road you are taking will not lead to your glory. For the Lord will hand Sisera over to a woman.'
The Lord turned to him and said, 'Go in this might of yours and save Israel from the hand of Midian. Haven't I sent you?'
Then David said to the Philistine, 'You come to me with a sword, a spear, and a javelin; but I come to you in the name of the Lord of Armies, the God of the armies of Israel, whom you have taunted.'

guide.summary: Elijah, Esther, Daniel, and Jonah demonstrate how God honors faithfulness even in the most extreme situations. Elijah confronted kings; Esther saved her people from genocide; Daniel refused compromise with idolatry; Jonah preached repentance even against his will. Their lives testify that no circumstance is so adverse that faithfulness to God cannot transform it.

keyVerses.text: Elijah came near to all the people and said, 'How long are you going to hesitate between two opinions? If the Lord is God, follow him. If Baal is god, follow him.'

Go, gather together all the Jews who are present in Susa, and fast for me. Don't eat or drink for three days, night or day. I and my young women will fast the same way. After that I will go in to the king, even though it is against the law; and if I perish, I perish.

If it is so, our God whom we serve is able to deliver us from the burning fiery furnace. He will deliver us out of your hand, O king. But even if he doesn't, let it be known to you, O king, that we will not serve your gods or worship the golden image that you have set up.
